risks: private is an audience restriction, not the disabled-context state required by acceptance; silently equating them can leak to owner's delegated agent or misrepresent the UI.
Mandatory emailContextVisibility on hide/unhide conflicts with optional emailContextEnabled update semantics and can re-enable disabled context if a default or stale snapshot is sent.
Target ingestion opt-out is underspecified and absent from published crm.setVisibility payload; presentation disable must not be used as a fake ingestion stop or OAuth revocation.
Name-matched Dossier touches are not entity links or authorization. Unknown/unavailable feed and failed notes search must not become authorized empty context.

Saved briefSessionId/assistant text and aggregate/search/notification caches can retain source bodies after disable/revoke; deleting raw source or merely hiding a Company row does not fix current read authorization.
Common contracts.ts/commands.ts/repository.ts and two proposed migration filenames have overlapping package ownership; independently writing them would introduce conflict/duplicate migrations.

Existing local dos-* cards do not carry canonical refs or server revisions. Shared visibility cutover requires accepted alias projection while retaining notes/promises/briefs and explicit standalone behavior.
Personal/team hidden precedence and Company-to-Contact cascade are normative decision points, not permission to delete children or change source grants.
Atomic command commit alone cannot protect stale snippets while asynchronous projections lag; synchronous current-policy read fence plus replay/epoch checks is required.

WP-36/WP-38 are not explicit WP-26 dependencies, but full native-agent/cache non-bypass acceptance still needs owner-approved real dispatcher/resolver integration; it cannot be deferred or marked N/A.
Working-tree integration is concurrent. Hash-bound evidence may become stale after wave0/dependency commits; this report is preflight only and no feature PASS or runtime receipt exists.
